edges.description: Cerebellar hypoplasia and atrophy underlie the cerebellar ataxia that names the syndrome.
Cerebellar hypoplasia is the imaging manifestation of this structural node.
Progressive cerebellar volume loss is the atrophic manifestation of this structural node.
Pontine hypoplasia is the brainstem manifestation of this structural node.
The brain malformation underlies seizures in a severely affected patient.

edges.limitations: Zebrafish crispants are mosaic and reflect acute knockdown rather than the constitutional biallelic hypomorphic state; the readout is a global reduction in head/eye size rather than isolated cerebellar or pontine hypoplasia, and no cardiac phenotype was reported.

nodes.description: Biallelic EXOSC5 variants (recurrent hypomorphic missense such as p.Thr114Ile plus null alleles including intragenic deletions and frameshifts) alter EXOSC5, a structural subunit of the RNA exosome. Some variants reduce RNA exosome function and alter interactions with other exosome subunits; the Slavotinek study concludes that disease mechanism varies with the specific variant. The nine-subunit exosome core (EXOSC1-9) is catalytically inactive and the 3' to 5' exoribonuclease activity is supplied by the associated DIS3 and EXOSC10 nucleases, so the GO:0000175 binding here represents the activity of the whole complex that EXOSC5 scaffolds rather than a catalytic function lost from EXOSC5 itself.
